title: I Was Locked Inside a Mall for 30 Days 🛍️
titleAlt: 30 Days Trapped: The Mall Doors Never Opened
description:
I was locked inside a mall for 30 days. This is my day-by-day diary of rules, allies and the shadows I could not explain. A fictional animated story.

#survival #animation #story #30days
topic: A narrator spends 30 days trapped in a locked mall with two allies

kapanis.soru: Who do you think is hiding in the dark?

satirlar.metin: Day thirty. The doors are still locked, and something just moved in the dark.
I am telling you this diary because I still do not know how it ends, and I need you to know what happened.
Let me go back to the start. It was a normal Friday evening.
The mall was loud and busy a minute earlier. Now every voice around me had gone quiet, and the silence felt heavier than any noise.
I was buying shoes when the lights flickered and a loud lock clicked.
I ran to the nearest door and pulled with all my strength. Nothing moved, not even a little.
Every exit was sealed. My phone had no signal.
I told myself to stay calm.
I counted the exits twice. Each one had the same metal shutter, and each one was cold under my hands.
Hey! Over here! I work at the shop. The system locked the whole building.
Mia saved me from panic. I was not alone.
She handed me a bottle of water and a granola bar. It was the kindest thing anyone had done for me all day.
Day two. Hunger kicked in, so we raided the food court.
Take only what we need. This has to last.
The shelves were full, but we did not know how long the lockdown would last. So we counted every can and every box.
We made rules. Ration the food. Sleep in shifts. Never split up.
Rule one kept us fair, rule two kept us rested, and rule three kept us alive. We repeated them every morning like a promise.
Day five. We built a camp from sofas and display beds.
Not bad. It almost feels like home.
We slept on soft mattresses, but I barely closed my eyes. Every small creak made my heart jump.
Then the power started to fail. The mall went dark every night.
In the dark, the mall sounded alive. Pipes clicked, vents sighed, and something far away kept tapping.
Day eight. A flashlight beam crossed the ceiling. We froze.
Mia gripped my sleeve. We held our breath and listened to the footsteps getting closer.
Easy. I am the night guard. I got locked in too.
Ben had a radio and a heavy ring of keys.
He had been locked in for two days, alone, walking the halls and talking to himself to stay sane.
The radio only catches static. But the security room has a map of every exit.
Then we find one.
Maps and keys gave us hope, and hope was the one thing we could not buy in any store.
Day twelve. We tried the roof door. It was welded shut by the lockdown.
We pushed and pulled and checked every bolt. The lockdown system was built to keep people out, and it worked just as well keeping us in.
Day sixteen. Food was running low and tempers were rising.
People can be brave for a week. Hunger and fear test them on the second week, and I saw it on every face.
We argue, we lose. Let's share the plan again.
I felt ashamed of raising my voice. Nobody wanted this, and the real enemy was the locked door, not each other.
We sat together and agreed. Everyone gets a job, and nobody sleeps hungry alone.
That night the camp felt warmer than it had in weeks. Small rules, shared food and honest words kept us together.
Day twenty-two. The power came back for ten seconds. A phone buzzed with one bar of signal.
I held it over my head and walked in a slow circle. Please, I whispered, just one more bar.
Send a message! Anything!
I typed with shaking hands: locked in mall, five of us.
The message went from sending to sent. Then the screen showed the tiny word delivered. We cried and laughed at the same time.
Five? We were only three. I looked up, and there were two new shadows near the stairs.
Those shadows were not part of our group. Whoever they were, they had been watching us for a long time.
Who is there?
Nobody answered. Then every light went out.
I do not know who was in the dark, or what they wanted. Part two begins with that answer.
